description: Backtests a betting angle or trend on every NFL game since 1999 against the closing number: record, win rate with a 95% interval, the exact chance a coin flip does as well, how it did in the last five seasons held out, season by season, and what the best of 20 random angles looks like at that sample, so a lucky trend is called noise. Filters: team, opponent, home/away, favorite/underdog, line range, total range, off a bye, opponent off a bye, short week, rest edge, division, prime time, weekday, Thanksgiving, week range, playoffs, dome/outdoors, temperature, wind, time zones travelled, miles, after a win/loss/blowout, referee. Bet against the spread, moneyline, over or under. For 'home dogs after a bye, real or noise', 'big road favourites off a loss', 'how do teams do on a short week', 'Thanksgiving road teams ATS'. Pass angles_tried if several angles were looked at, to correct for the search.

after.description: What happened in the team's previous game.

angles_tried.description: How many angles were tried before this one (corrects the p-value for searching).

bet.description: What to bet (default ats: against the spread).

line_max.description: Side's own line at most this.

line_min.description: Side's own line at least this (e.g. 3 = dogs of +3 or more; -7 = favourites of 7 or less).

rest_edge_min.description: At least this many more rest days than the opponent.

team.description: Team: abbreviation, city or nickname, e.g. DAL, Dallas, Cowboys.

name: backtest_angle
title: Is this betting angle real or noise? Backtest a trend against the spread since 1999
